title: Was the thrust-to-weight ceiling of 4 what made rotor cant look good?
lede: does raising the TWR ceiling from 4 to 6 and 8 erase the cant advantage? No: cant to 35° still beats no cant in 5 of 5 seeds at three measured propeller c values, by 1.5–3.0° at ceiling 8 (1.6–3.4° at 4); the optimiser stops near TWR 5 without cant.
summary: Follow-up to codesign-aero-cant-twr, whose no-cant design sat on its assumed TWR ceiling of 4. Same joint CMA-ES co-design (1920 evaluations, 5 seeds, 64 held-out episodes, $300 cap, c at the 10th, 50th and 90th percentile of measured UIUC propeller data) with the ceiling at 4, 6 and 8. Raising it from 4 to 6 improves the no-cant design by 0.2–0.35° and the optimiser then picks TWR 4.9–5.1; from 6 to 8 nothing changes (within ±0.1°). Cant to 35° still beats no cant in 5 of 5 seeds at every c and ceiling, by 1.5–3.0° at ceiling 8, so the earlier gap was overstated by 0.1–0.4°. Limits: the interior optimum comes from inherited, assumed motor mass and cost fits (not a catalogue), attitude steps only, no position hold, no hardware.
